_source: PRIXEL Mono specimen booklet (reference/prixel_mono_booklet_-_download.pdf), INVENTORY page — corrected against a photograph of the printed page.
_note: Multi-character keys are one physical piece that becomes another character when rotated (C/U, H/I, M/W, N/Z, 6/9). Diacritics sit in the cell ABOVE the letter. There is NO acute accent - only tilde, grave, circumflex.

colon upright; rotated it is a DIAERESIS - place above a letter for a/e/i/o/u umlauts

_diacritics.NOT available: acute ´ - so é, á, í, ó, ú cannot be set. crème and brûl work; the é of brûlée does not.
_diacritics.placement: the mark sits at the BOTTOM of its cell, so the piece goes in the row ABOVE the letter. Rotating a grave to fake an acute moves the mark to the top of the cell, away from the letter, so it does not work.
_diacritics.cost: an accented line needs a clear row above it, and with 2 of each mark you cannot accent more than two letters of the same type per plate.
